subject: Human Evolution
title: High-Altitude Genes
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on High-Altitude Genes.

hook.text: Tibetans, Andean highlanders, and Ethiopian plateau dwellers all adapted to thin air—using different genes.

buildup.text: At 4,000+ meters, oxygen levels drop 40%. Without adaptation, altitude sickness, edema, and death follow.

discovery.text: Tibetans use the Denisovan EPAS1 gene to avoid overproducing red blood cells—preventing deadly thickened blood.

twist.text: Andeans took a different path: they evolved larger lungs and higher hemoglobin concentrations.

climax.text: Same problem, different solutions. Convergent evolution found multiple ways to breathe on the roof of the world.

punchline.text: Three populations solved the same puzzle differently.

quiz.question: How do Tibetans adapt to high altitude differently from Andeans?
options: Tibetans use EPAS1 to limit red blood cells; Andeans have larger lungs
Both groups use the same gene
